body.estimand_functional: \(\Theta_I(\psi;\mathbf z)=[D_1(\mathbf z),U_1(\mathbf z)],\quad U_k=H_{\mathbf z_k}(U_{k+1}),\quad D_k=h_{\mathbf z_k}(D_{k+1}),\quad U_{K+1}=D_{K+1}=0\)

sampling_model.design: Balanced two-arm baseline randomization with fixed inspection grid \(0=t_0<\cdots<t_K=T\).
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the finite grouped first-event law \(\pi\).
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is known; under the prespecified ceiling \(L\), factual and hybrid survival is at least \(e^{-2LT}>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No hazard is estimated. The empirical nuisance is the \(m=2(2K+1)\)-cell multinomial vector \(\widehat\pi\), which is inverted through \(\mathcal C_n\).
sampling_model.randomness: Sampling randomness arises only from independent subjects; the inspection grid, externally calibrated ceiling \(L\), conservative ceiling \(\bar L\), and causal component model are fixed before analyzing the grouped outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under treatment decomposition and dismissible component conditions, separable event risks are identified by a discrete-time g-functional.
With resolved event times, the continuous-time separable cause-1 risk is the cross-arm cause-specific hazard integral and admits influence-function estimation.
Discrete competing-risk latent-duration bounds can be computed from a sequential system of nonlinear equalities and inequalities.
Occupation-measure LMI relaxations provide monotone lower bounds converging to a nonlinear optimal-control value under the paper's compactness and convexity conditions.
A smooth bounded-control problem can have optimal chattering at a singular junction.
Inverting a covering collection yields a finite-sample multinomial confidence region with coverage at least the nominal level.

body.tldr: Scheduled inspections identify factual competing-event bin probabilities but erase the within-bin ordering needed to splice the cause-1 hazard from arm 1 with the cause-2 hazard from arm 0. Conditional on an externally calibrated ceiling \(L\) imposed uniformly across the four cause-by-arm hazards, disclosed as a novel maintained sensitivity restriction, the sharp component-risk interval is characterized by one-bin incidence-survival support envelopes and an exact backward recursion; replacing \(L\) by a conservative \(\bar L\ge L\) can only enlarge the interval. Whether every envelope extremum admits a parameter-uniform bound on the number of shared constant-control subintervals remains open; the note specifies a positive-cell two-cycle constrained-Hessian kill test for that question. The matched mesh-width theorem and finite-sample multinomial inversion do not claim such a finite representation.

project_justification.gap: Resolved-time separable-effect theory identifies the cross-arm hazard integral, and discrete competing-risk partial-identification theory treats latent-duration distributions, but neither characterizes the sharp grouped-data component-risk frontier conditional on a transparently calibrated intensity ceiling or its monotone sensitivity expansion when that ceiling is relaxed.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the exact active-ceiling one-bin incidence-survival support envelope under two simultaneous factual endpoint constraints, including whether every optimizer can be compressed to a parameter-uniform finite switching word and whether the claim survives an exact positive-cell two-cycle Hessian test.
project_justification.fill: The project treats \(L\) as an externally calibrated maintained restriction, derives nested identified sets under \(L\) and \(\bar L\), and constructs the attainable survival-flow frontier. It formulates—without resolving—the question whether a parameter-uniform finite shared-piece bound exists, together with the specified cycle-compression predicate. It composes local envelopes into globally sharp endpoints, proves the matched inspection-mesh modulus, and projects a simultaneous multinomial confidence region through the certified endpoint map.

body.related_work: StensrudYoungDidelezRobinsHernan2022, Sections 5--6 and Supplementary Appendix B, motivates treatment decomposition and proves a discrete-time identifying g-functional under dismissible component conditions; its observation model fixes within-period order and does not make a numerical intensity ceiling an identifying parameter. MartinussenStensrud2023, Sections 2.3--2.4 and Appendix 8.1, supplies the resolved-time cross-arm hazard integral and influence-function benchmark; grouped bin triples do not recover its integrands, and its bounded-intensity regularity does not calibrate the common ceiling that determines the present identified set. The present model is the no-covariate, no-additional-censoring, balanced-randomization specialization of that hazard-splicing setup, augmented by grouped observation and a single pointwise cap imposed uniformly across the four hazards; finite-mesh sharpness is claimed only for \(\mathcal M(\mathbf z)\), not for the full published class. Accordingly, \(L\) is disclosed here as a novel maintained sensitivity-model restriction, calibrated before analysis from a scientifically certified envelope in an external exact-time registry or audited event-trigger system, with \(\bar L\) providing a conservative nested-set analysis. StensrudHernanTchetgenRobinsDidelezYoung2021, Sections 6, 8, and 10, generalizes the g-formula and applies it to monthly kidney injury and death in SPRINT while describing within-interval ordering as practically negligible on fine grids. Kim2023CompetingRisks, Sections 2--4, formulates a sequential nonlinear sharp-bounds problem for discretely measured latent competing durations, but the target and feasible set are not hazard-spliced component risks. LasserreHenrionPrieurTrelat2008, Theorems 2.3 and 3.6, converts nonlinear control to occupation measures and convergent moment relaxations; convergence does not recover an exact ordinary control with uniformly many pieces. ZhuTrelatCerf2016 shows that Pontryagin conditions alone do not rule out chattering, while BayerTeichmann2006 gives finite atomic moment representations that do not preserve chronological survival dynamics. MaathuisHudgens2011 and SchmidBerger2021 describe grouped competing-risk inference for factual incidence functions. ChafaiConcordet2009, Theorem 2.2, gives the input-law covering-region argument used for finite-sample inversion. FangSantos2019 and FirpoGalvaoParker2023 explain why derivative-aware resampling is the appropriate later refinement at endpoint ties, but derivative theory is not substituted for exact set coverage here. The 2026 ParkSuk2026 preprint concerns two-arm versus four-arm identification and estimation, not grouped continuous-time hazard frontiers.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact five-piece positive-cell family and fixed-grid optimizations establish feasible support values only. The unresolved phase has both nuisance hazards saturated and negative factual-incidence multipliers; first-order switching equations permit repeated four-corner cycles. The mandatory early-kill instance fixes a positive-cell law induced by two equal-duration cycles and asks whether the exact constrained Lagrangian Hessian yields an endpoint-preserving deletion exchange or a strict interior-over-boundary obstruction. Excluding a simultaneous interior singular arc by the Goh condition and compressing isolated single-control singular arcs does not by itself settle that sign predicate or bound the number of globally optimal bang cycles.
body.honest_scope: Factual-bin compatibility, compact attainment, interval sharpness, backward gluing, ceiling-sensitivity nesting, the inactive-ceiling reduction, matched mesh order, and confidence-region coverage are supporting claims to prove. A parameter-uniform finite-piece representation of the exact active-ceiling frontier remains an open computational-structure extension; the sharp-set characterization, global recursion, and matched mesh theorem do not depend on it. Its first kill test is the fully specified positive-cell two-cycle constrained-Hessian problem. The model maintains hazard-component splicing and a common ceiling \(L\) externally calibrated before analysis; the ceiling is not a standard separable-effects implication, and conclusions are conditional on its validity. Reporting \(\bar L\ge L\) gives a nested conservative interval but does not eliminate this sensitivity restriction. The model does not assert latent independence, add covariates, address loss to follow-up, or claim a validated SPRINT reanalysis. In the resolved-time or vanishing-mesh special case the interval must collapse to the published continuous-time separable-risk functional.
